column1: How a sixteenth-century warship was recovered from the seabed
column2: 一艘16世纪的战船是怎样从海底打捞上来的。

column1: On 19 July 1545, English and French fleets were engaged in a sea battle off the coast of southern England in the area of water called the Solent, between Portsmouth and the Isle of Wight.
column2: 1545年7月19日，英法舰队在英格兰南部外海的索伦特海峡交战，这片水域位于朴次茅斯和怀特岛之间。
column6: off the coast of|在……附近海域

column1: Among the English vessels was a warship by the name of Mary Rose.
column2: 英方船只中有一艘名叫“玛丽玫瑰号”的战船。

column1: Built in Portsmouth some 35 years earlier, she had had a long and successful fighting career, and was a favourite of King Henry VIII.
column2: 这艘船约35年前在朴次茅斯建成。它长年服役，战绩卓著，深得亨利八世国王喜爱。
column4: some 35 years earlier|约三十五年前

column1: Accounts of what happened to the ship vary: while witnesses agree that she was not hit by the French, some maintain that she was outdated, overladen and sailing too low in the water, others that she was mishandled by undisciplined crew.
column2: 这艘船究竟遭遇了什么，众说纷纭。目击者一致认定它没被法军击中，但有人认为它已老旧过时，又超载，以致船身吃水太深；也有人说，是纪律松弛的船员操船失当。
column8: sailing too low in the water|吃水太深

column1: What is undisputed, however, is that the Mary Rose sank into the Solent that day, taking at least 500 men with her.
column2: 但毫无争议的是，那一天玛丽玫瑰号沉入索伦特海峡，至少500人随船罹难。
column6: taking at least 500 men with her|至少五百人随船罹难

column1: After the battle, attempts were made to recover the ship, but these failed.
column2: 战斗结束后，人们曾试图打捞这艘船，却没能成功。

column1: The Mary Rose came to rest on the seabed, lying on her starboard (right) side at an angle of approximately 60 degrees.
column2: 玛丽玫瑰号最终停在海床上，以大约60度的倾角侧卧在右舷一侧。
column6: at an angle of|以……的角度

column1: The hull (the body of the ship) acted as a trap for the sand and mud carried by Solent currents.
column2: 船体像个捕集器，截住了索伦特海峡水流带来的沙和泥。

column1: As a result, the starboard side filled rapidly, leaving the exposed port (left) side to be eroded by marine organisms and mechanical degradation.
column2: 结果，右舷一侧很快被泥沙填满，裸露的左舷则在海洋生物作用和机械磨损下逐渐被侵蚀。

column1: Because of the way the ship sank, nearly all of the starboard half survived intact.
column2: 得益于船沉没时的姿态，几乎整个右舷半部都完好地保存了下来。

column1: During the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, the entire site became covered with a layer of hard grey clay, which minimised further erosion.
column2: 在17和18世纪间，整处遗址逐渐被一层坚硬的灰色黏土覆盖，使后续侵蚀降到了最低。
column5: hard grey clay|坚硬的灰色黏土

column1: Then, on 16 June 1836, some fishermen in the Solent found that their equipment was caught on an underwater obstruction, which turned out to be the Mary Rose.
column2: 1836年6月16日，索伦特海峡的几名渔民发现渔具被水下障碍物钩住了，那处障碍物后来证实就是玛丽玫瑰号。
column7: turned out to be|后来证明是

column1: Diver John Deane happened to be exploring another sunken ship nearby, and the fishermen approached him, asking him to free their gear.
column2: 潜水员约翰·迪恩当时碰巧正在附近探查另一艘沉船，渔民便找到他，请他帮忙解开渔具。
column7: free their gear|解开他们的渔具

column1: Deane dived down, and found the equipment caught on a timber protruding slightly from the seabed.
column2: 迪恩潜入水中，发现渔具勾在一根略微突出海床的木材上。

column1: Exploring further, he uncovered several other timbers and a bronze gun.
column2: 继续探查时，他又发现了几根木构件和一门青铜炮。

column1: Deane continued diving on the site intermittently until 1840, recovering several more guns, two bows, various timbers, part of a pump and various other small finds.
column2: 直到1840年，迪恩仍断断续续来到遗址潜水，又捞出了几门炮、两张弓、多根木构件、一个泵的部件以及其他各类小物件。

column1: The Mary Rose then faded into obscurity for another hundred years.
column2: 之后，玛丽玫瑰号又沉寂了整整一个世纪，逐渐被人淡忘。
column3: faded into obscurity|逐渐被人淡忘

column1: But in 1965, military historian and amateur diver Alexander McKee, in conjunction with the British Sub-Aqua Club, initiated a project called ‘Solent Ships’.
column2: 但在1965年，军事史学家兼业余潜水员亚历山大·麦基与英国潜水俱乐部合作，发起了“索伦特船只”项目。

column1: While on paper this was a plan to examine a number of known wrecks in the Solent, what McKee really hoped for was to find the Mary Rose.
column2: 从纸面上看，项目计划考察索伦特海峡中已知的几处沉船遗址；麦基心里真正希望的，却是找到玛丽玫瑰号。

column1: Ordinary search techniques proved unsatisfactory, so McKee entered into collaboration with Harold E. Edgerton, professor of electrical engineering at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
column2: 常规搜索方法的效果并不理想，于是麦基开始与麻省理工学院电气工程教授哈罗德·埃杰顿合作。
column3: Ordinary search techniques|常规搜索方法
column5: entered into collaboration with|开始与……合作
column7: Massachusetts Institute of Technology|麻省理工学院

column1: In 1967, Edgerton’s side-scan sonar systems revealed a large, unusually shaped object, which McKee believed was the Mary Rose.
column2: 1967年，埃杰顿的侧扫声呐系统探测到一个形状异常的大型物体，麦基认为那就是玛丽玫瑰号。
column3: side-scan sonar systems|侧扫声呐系统

column1: Further excavations revealed stray pieces of timber and an iron gun.
column2: 进一步发掘又发现了零散的木构件和一门铁炮。

column1: But the climax to the operation came when, on 5 May 1971, part of the ship’s frame was uncovered.
column2: 这次行动的高潮出现在1971年5月5日，那天，船体骨架的一部分重见天日。

column1: McKee and his team now knew for certain that they had found the wreck, but were as yet unaware that it also housed a treasure trove of beautifully preserved artefacts.
column2: 至此，麦基和团队终于确信他们找到了这艘沉船，却还不知道里面藏着一批保存极佳的珍贵文物。
column5: as yet unaware|当时仍未意识到

column1: Interest in the project grew, and in 1979, The Mary Rose Trust was formed, with Prince Charles as its President and Dr Margaret Rule its Archaeological Director.
column2: 人们对项目的兴趣日增。1979年，玛丽玫瑰号信托基金会成立，由查尔斯王子出任会长，玛格丽特·鲁尔博士出任考古主管。

column1: The decision whether or not to salvage the wreck was not an easy one, although an excavation in 1978 had shown that it might be possible to raise the hull.
column2: 1978年的发掘虽说明船体有可能被吊起，但是否打捞沉船，仍是一项难以作出的决定。

column1: While the original aim was to raise the hull if at all feasible, the operation was not given the go-ahead until January 1982, when all the necessary information was available.
column2: 起初的目标是，只要可行，就把船体吊上来。但这项行动等到1982年1月所有必要信息齐备后，才获得批准。
column4: if at all feasible|只要有可能做到

column1: An important factor in trying to salvage the Mary Rose was that the remaining hull was an open shell.
column2: 试图打捞玛丽玫瑰号时，有个重要因素必须考虑：残存的船体是一个敞开的外壳。

column1: This led to an important decision being taken: namely to carry out the lifting operation in three very distinct stages.
column2: 因此，人们作出了一项重要决定，把起吊作业分为三个截然不同的阶段。

column1: The hull was attached to a lifting frame via a network of bolts and lifting wires.
column2: 船体通过一套由螺栓和起吊钢索构成的连接系统固定在起吊架上。
column5: via a network of|通过一套相连的

column1: The problem of the hull being sucked back downwards into the mud was overcome by using 12 hydraulic jacks.
column2: 淤泥会产生向下的吸力，把船体吸回泥中。工程人员使用12个液压千斤顶解决了这一难题。

column1: These raised it a few centimetres over a period of several days, as the lifting frame rose slowly up its four legs.
column2: 几天内，起吊架沿着四条支腿缓慢上升，这些千斤顶将船体抬高了几厘米。
column5: over a period of several days|在几天时间里

column1: It was only when the hull was hanging freely from the lifting frame, clear of the seabed and the suction effect of the surrounding mud, that the salvage operation progressed to the second stage.
column2: 直到船体完全脱离海床和周围淤泥的吸力，自由地悬挂在起吊架下方，打捞行动才进入第二阶段。

column1: In this stage, the lifting frame was fixed to a hook attached to a crane, and the hull was lifted completely clear of the seabed and transferred underwater into the lifting cradle.
column2: 在这一阶段，起吊架被固定到起重机的吊钩上，船体被完全吊离海床，随后在水下移入起吊承托架。
column6: lifted completely clear of|完全吊离

column1: This required precise positioning to locate the legs into the ‘stabbing guides’ of the lifting cradle.
column2: 这需要精确定位，才能将支腿插入承托架的“插接导向槽”内。

column1: The lifting cradle was designed to fit the hull using archaeological survey drawings, and was fitted with air bags to provide additional cushioning for the hull’s delicate timber framework.
column2: 人们依据考古测绘图，设计出与船体贴合的起吊承托架；架上还装有气囊，为船体脆弱的木质骨架提供额外缓冲。

column1: The third and final stage was to lift the entire structure into the air, by which time the hull was also supported from below.
column2: 第三个也是最后一个阶段，是把整套结构吊到空中；此时，船体下方也已得到支撑。
column3: third and final stage|第三也是最后一个阶段
column6: supported from below|从下方得到支撑

column1: Finally, on 11 October 1982, millions of people around the world held their breath as the timber skeleton of the Mary Rose was lifted clear of the water, ready to be returned home to Portsmouth.
column2: 终于，1982年10月11日，世界各地数百万人屏息凝望着玛丽玫瑰号的木质骨架吊离水面，准备重返它的故乡朴次茅斯。
column5: lifted clear of the water|吊离水面
